title: An inseparable element produces a nilpotent after algebraic-closure base change
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $K/k$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $\bar{k}$ be an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\alpha\in K$. If the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$ is inseparable, then $K\otimes_k\bar{k}$ contains a nonzero nilpotent element and is therefore not reduced.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030V (algebra-lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension), together with Tag 030W

proof.text: Let P be the minimal polynomial of alpha and Q its coefficient extension to kbar. Integrality makes P monic, so Q is nonzero. Polynomial.separable_map shows that Q is inseparable.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso], namely IntermediateField.adjoinRootEquivAdjoin, to embed AdjoinRoot P into K. Flatness over the field k preserves this injection after tensoring with kbar (Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap).

AdjoinRoot.tensorAlgEquiv identifies kbar tensor_k AdjoinRoot P with AdjoinRoot of P mapped to kbar tensor_k k. AdjoinRoot.mapAlgEquiv applied to Algebra.TensorProduct.rid identifies this with AdjoinRoot Q, that is kbar[T]/(Q).

Suppose K tensor_k kbar is reduced. Commutativity of tensor products and the preceding injection imply that AdjoinRoot Q is reduced. Ideal.isRadical_iff_quotient_reduced and isRadical_iff_span_singleton make Q radical. As Q is nonzero, it is squarefree; PerfectField.separable_iff_squarefree over the algebraically closed field kbar makes Q separable, a contradiction.
Apply exists_isNilpotent_of_not_isReduced to obtain a nonzero nilpotent, and pair its existence with the already proved failure of reducedness.
